scope.description: One-row deepening tranche for Wooper, the CoroCoro Comic January 2000 issue insert released December 15, 1999, emphasizing the Gold/Silver launch moment, CoroCoro as Johto-era delivery rail, Ken Sugimori art, glossy unnumbered promo identity, and traps against later Wooper cards or generic CoroCoro promo memory.
in_scope: CoroCoro Comic January 2000 issue insert release dossier

chase_cards.name: Wooper
chase_cards.why: This row is a chase because it catches a newly arrived Johto Pokemon in CoroCoro's hands just weeks after Gold/Silver launched in Japan; modest creature, huge moment.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Bulbapedia, Pokumon, and PokeBoon credit this Wooper to Ken Sugimori; in this specific row the importance is not a showy composition, but the mainline Pokemon visual language being carried directly into a magazine bonus card.

claims.text: The local catalog models the CoroCoro Comic January 2000 issue insert as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Wooper at source index 146.
Bulbapedia's unnumbered promotional list places Wooper in the CoroCoro Comic January 2000 issue insert, released December 15, 1999.
Pokumon and PokeBoon both describe the card as a CoroCoro / magazine-insert promo, and Pokumon further tags it as glossy and non-holo.
The official Pokemon site lists Pokemon Gold and Silver as released in Japan on November 21, 1999, less than a month before this CoroCoro insert date.
Because the row appears immediately after the Japanese Gold/Silver launch, this Wooper functions as a magazine-era Johto arrival marker rather than merely a standalone common Pokemon promo.
Bulbapedia's Wooper CoroCoro promo page credits the illustration to Ken Sugimori.
Pokumon and PokeBoon also list Ken Sugimori as the illustrator for this CoroCoro Wooper promo.
Bulbapedia's Wooper promo page says the card carries the Gold, Silver, to a New World... symbol and bottom-border text reading CoroCoro Comic January issue bonus card.

Agents should preserve the CoroCoro January 2000 insert route, December 15 1999 date, glossy unnumbered promo signal, Ken Sugimori credit, Gold/Silver symbol, and January-issue bonus-card border text before accepting a match.

steps: Confirm the release route is CoroCoro Comic January 2000 issue insert, released December 15, 1999.
Confirm the card is Wooper / ウパー as an unnumbered Japanese promotional card, not a numbered expansion Wooper or later Wooper reprint.
Preserve Ken Sugimori as illustrator and avoid replacing the credit with a generic unknown-artist value.
Check for glossy CoroCoro magazine-insert stock when scan and seller evidence allow.
Check for the Gold, Silver, to a New World... promotional symbol.

narrative.human_title: Wooper: a little Johto creature tucked into CoroCoro
narrative.why_it_matters: This is not a trophy-card roar. It is something quieter and, in its own way, better for the history layer: a new Johto Pokemon arriving through the magazine pipeline while Gold and Silver were still fresh on Japanese shelves. Wooper feels like a small creature, but the assembly around it is large: CoroCoro's kid-facing distribution, Sugimori's official visual language, the Gold/Silver symbol, and the physical pleasure of a glossy bonus card. It is Pokemon turning the page from Kanto to Johto in a child's hands.

The card's art significance is its clean Sugimori creature read: a Johto species carried into the TCG promo stream in the same official visual grammar collectors already knew from the games and guide material.
The card should be checked as the CoroCoro January 2000 issue bonus Wooper with the Gold/Silver symbol and bonus-card border text, not merely as any Japanese Wooper.

narrative.why_it_matters: Wooper is exactly the kind of card a collector can miss if the catalog only worships trophies. It is a little blue creature from the moment the Pokemon world doubled: Gold and Silver had just opened Johto, and CoroCoro put one of those new faces directly into the magazine stack. The appeal is not drama. It is intimacy: Sugimori's simple character language, glossy stock, a Gold/Silver symbol, and the feeling that a new region had slipped into your binder before the rest of the world caught up.
